explain.say: Picture the wide grassy savanna in Kenya or Tanzania. A zebra munches grass, and a lion watches from the bushes. Who eats whom? A food chain shows it, with arrows that mean is eaten by. And see the Sun lighting up at the very start? It powers everything.

faq.a: A food chain shows who eats whom, step by step. The arrows mean is eaten by, and they show energy moving from plants to animals, for example grass to zebra to lion.
asks: What do the arrows in a food chain mean?

faq.q: Why does every food chain start with a plant?
faq.a: Plants are producers: they make their own food from sunlight. Animals cannot, so they need plants, or animals that ate plants, for their energy.

faq.q: Why are there fewer lions than zebras?
faq.a: At each step most energy is used up for moving, breathing and keeping warm, and only about a tenth passes on. So there is only enough energy for a few lions at the top.

faq.q: What happens when the lion dies?
faq.a: Vultures, insects, fungi and bacteria break the body down. The goodness goes back into the soil and helps grass grow, so nothing is wasted.
A predator is an animal that hunts and eats other animals, called its prey. A lion is a predator and a zebra is its prey.

facts: On average only about 10 percent of energy passes from one step of a food chain to the next.
Plants are producers: they capture energy from sunlight by photosynthesis.

quiz.say: In the chain grass, zebra, lion, which one is the producer?
quiz.why: Grass makes its own food from sunlight, so it is the producer.

wrong.1: The zebra eats the grass, so it is a consumer.
wrong.2: The lion eats zebras, so it is a consumer and a predator.

quiz.say: What does an arrow in a food chain mean?
quiz.show: An arrow in a food chain means…
quiz.why: The arrow means is eaten by, showing energy passing along.

wrong.1: Food chains are about eating, not friendship.
wrong.2: Size does not matter: a tiny insect can eat a big leaf.
